originalTitle: Bill Miller's investing strategy: How the legendary fund manager outperformed the market for 15 straight years
simplifiedContent: Bill Miller, a well-known investor, did better than the overall stock market for 15 years in a row. He achieved this by using a combination of strategies, including looking for undervalued companies and being patient for a long time. Miller focuses on finding companies with strong financials and waiting for their stock prices to reflect their true worth. This approach helped him make successful investments by taking advantage of times when the market overreacted to news. By following this strategy, Miller was able to consistently outperform the market, making his investments more profitable.

originalTitle: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank posts Rs 34 crore Q1 loss; asset quality stress persists
simplifiedContent: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank recently reported that it lost Rs 34 crore in the first quarter of the year. This is the fifth time in a row that the bank has reported a loss, which means it has been spending more money than it has been making for a while now. The bank's losses are partly because some of the loans it gave out are not being paid back, which is a problem known as "asset quality stress". The bank's bad loans, or non-performing assets, are still very high at 6.1%, which is a concern. The good news is that the bank's loss is smaller than it was before, but it still has a lot of work to do to get back on track.

originalTitle: Muthoot Finance reports 25% rise in Q1 profit, announces leadership transition
simplifiedContent: Muthoot Finance, a company that lends money to people using their gold as security, made a profit of Rs 2,550 crore in the first quarter of the year. This is 25% more than they made in the same period last year. The company's gold loan business is doing very well, which is why their profit is up. The company is also getting a new managing director, Alexander George Muthoot, who will take over on October 1 if the company's shareholders agree. This news matters because it shows how well the company is doing and who will be in charge in the future.

originalTitle: Week Ahead: Wall Street eyes US jobs data, SpaceX debut earnings and Disney results
simplifiedContent: This week, investors are waiting to see how many new jobs were created in the US in July. This information is important because it will help them understand what might happen to interest rates in the coming months. Interest rates affect how much it costs to borrow money, which can impact the stock market. Investors will also be paying attention to the financial results of two big companies: SpaceX, which is reporting its earnings for the first time, and Disney. These reports will give investors a better idea of how these companies are doing and whether they want to invest in them.

originalTitle: Sebi order against Zee likely to delay planned  ₹3,143-crore fundraise
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has taken action against Zee, which means they can't buy or sell securities for a while. This is likely to delay Zee's plan to raise ₹3,143 crore in funds. In simple terms, Zee was planning to collect a large amount of money from investors, but now that might not happen on time. This matters because Zee needs this money, and the delay could affect their plans. The Sebi order is essentially a restriction on Zee's activities in the stock market for a certain period.

originalTitle: Yen Traders Brace for More Intervention With US at Japan’s Side
simplifiedContent: Some important people who trade currencies are closely watching what happens next with the Japanese yen. Last week, Japan and the US worked together to help the yen's value go back up, and now these traders think they might do it again. This could happen when markets open in Asia on Monday. The traders are paying close attention because they want to know what will happen to the yen's value, which can affect their investments. This matters because it could lead to big changes in the currency market.
